correctness.rationale: A shortest path in a fixed cycle layer cannot move in the path coordinate. Four marks in such a layer obstruct both arcs between an alternating pair, proving the upper bound 3s. For the stated M, h=floor(t/3)>=2s separates the three width-s windows and makes all marked columns distinct. In one window a move in the starting column followed by a move in the destination row has length 2|a-b| and no marked interior. Across windows orient from one to its cyclic successor. The forward column distance is h+b-a, or h+r+b-a across the wrap with r=t-3h. Thus t-2D is at least h+r-2(s-1) before the wrap and h-r-2(s-1)>=0 at the wrap. Equality is harmless: the selected arc is still shortest. Switch rows in the empty column immediately after the first window; each row segment encounters only its own marked endpoint. This also works when the endpoints have identical first coordinates. The resulting length is D+|a-b|. Independently, reachable-set expansion on the graph with other marks removed checked 699 endpoint pairs including all three residues at s=3 and s=5; replay: python3 -I /tmp/opencode/frozen_audit_small_checks.py, visibility(). These finite checks corroborate the path argument; frozen scripts were inspected, not run.
residual_risks: No necessity, optimal cutoff, or conclusion outside the stated parameter domain was audited; the finite computation alone cannot establish the theorem.
